match.reason: The bank point teaches epidemiology, the study of health patterns in populations, and does not cover non-government organisations or community-based program delivery, so no existing point teaches the new idea.

draft.title: Non-government organisations
card: A non-government organisation (NGO) is a group that is not run by a government. Many are charities that raise money from donations and use it for a cause.
Many NGOs run health and development programs. Examples include vaccination drives, clean water projects and training for health workers.
NGOs often work closely with local communities. They may employ local staff and ask residents what they need, so programs fit local conditions.
Some NGOs are small and work in one region. Others are large and work in many countries. Examples include Oxfam, World Vision and Médecins Sans Frontières.
draft.remember: An NGO is a non-government group, often a charity, that runs programs and often works closely with local communities.

a.q: Which description best fits a non-government organisation?
opts: A charity that runs a clean water project in a village
A government department that sends funds to another country
A body of many governments that sets health rules
A company that sells medicine to make a profit
a.why: An NGO is not run by a government, and many are charities that run programs. A government department is the opposite of non-government. A body of many governments is also government-led, so it is not an NGO.
a.clue: Look for a group that is not run by any government.

b.q: An NGO plans to cut child illness in a remote town. Which step best shows it working closely with the local community?
opts: It asks residents what health problems matter most to them
It writes the plan overseas and sends staff to follow it
It runs the program from a city office far from the town
It lets a foreign government choose the program's goals
b.why: Asking residents what they need is a direct way of working with the community, so the program fits local conditions. Writing the plan overseas and sending staff to follow it leaves residents out, so it is not close community work.
b.clue: Which step involves the people who live in the town?

a.best: A charity that runs a clean water project in a village

b.best: It asks residents what health problems matter most to them

problems.detail: The card defines an NGO only as 'a group that is not run by a government'. That definition leaves out that NGOs are not-for-profit, so a private company would fit it.

The clue 'Look for a group that is not run by any government' does not rule out the distractor 'A company that sells medicine to make a profit', which is also not government-run. The card gives students no basis for rejecting it, and the why does not explain why a for-profit company is not an NGO.

proposal.title: Non-government organisations
card: A non-government organisation (NGO) is a not-for-profit group that is independent of government. The money it raises goes back into its cause, not to owners or shareholders.
Many NGOs are charities funded by donations, and some also get government grants. Governments do not run them. A business that sells goods to make profits for its owners is not an NGO.
Many NGOs run health and development programs, such as vaccination drives, clean water projects and training for health workers. Examples include Oxfam, World Vision and Médecins Sans Frontières.
NGOs often work closely with local communities. They may employ local staff and ask residents what they need, so programs fit local conditions.
proposal.remember: Not run by government, not run for profit: NGOs put their money into programs, often shaped with local people.

opts: A charity that runs a clean water project in a village
A government department that sends funds to another country
A body of many governments that sets health rules
A company that sells medicine to make a profit

a.clue: Check two things: who runs it, and where its money goes.
